title: HTML Forms — Complete Fundamentals
goal: Build a labelled form with the right input types and submit behaviour.

topics.title: A form needs a method and an action
topics.body: `action` batata hai data kahan jaayega aur `method` batata hai kaise. GET URL me data bhejta hai, POST body me.
topics.code:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<body>
  <form action="/register" method="post">
    <label for="name">Name</label>
    <input id="name" name="name" type="text">
    <button type="submit">Send</button>
  </form>
</body>
</html>

topics.title: label for connects text to the input
topics.body: `for` attribute input ki `id` se match hona chahiye. Clicking the label focuses the input, and screen readers announce the pair.
topics.code:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<body>
  <label for="email">Email</label>
  <input id="email" name="email" type="email">
</body>
</html>

topics.title: Input types choose a keyboard and validation
topics.body: `type="email"`, `tel`, `date` aur `number` mobile keyboard aur basic validation badalte hain, lekin server-side check phir bhi zaroori hai.
topics.code:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<body>
  <label for="phone">Phone</label>
  <input id="phone" name="phone" type="tel">
  <label for="dob">Date of birth</label>
  <input id="dob" name="dob" type="date">
</body>
</html>

debug.title: A label with no matching id
debug.error: Broken label association: for points at a missing id, so clicking the label does nothing and the input has no accessible name.

debug.title: A submit button that does not submit
debug.error: Missing type: inside a form the default is submit, but an explicit type prevents surprises when the button is reused elsewhere.

tasks.title: Registration form
tasks.statement: Build a form with name, email and password fields, each with a matching label and a submit button.
tasks.solution:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<body>
  <form action="/register" method="post">
    <label for="name">Name</label>
    <input id="name" name="name" type="text" required>
    <label for="email">Email</label>
    <input id="email" name="email" type="email" required>
    <label for="password">Password</label>
    <input id="password" name="password" type="password" required>
    <button type="submit">Create account</button>
  </form>
</body>
</html>

interviewBank.q: What is the difference between GET and POST?
interviewBank.answer: GET appends the data to the URL, which makes it visible, bookmarkable and length-limited. POST sends it in the request body, which suits state-changing submissions and larger payloads.

interviewBank.q: Why does every input need a name attribute?
interviewBank.answer: The name is the key submitted with the value. Without it the field is not included in the form data at all.

defenseBank.q: A learner complains that clicking the label does nothing.
defenseBank.answer: I check that for matches an id exactly; a typo silently breaks the association.

defenseBank.q: Why not rely on placeholder instead of label?
defenseBank.answer: A placeholder disappears as soon as typing starts and is not a reliable accessible name. The label stays visible and is announced.

mcqBank.q: Which method sends form data in the URL query string?
mcqBank.why: GET appends the fields to the URL.

mcqBank.q: Which attribute associates a label with an input?
mcqBank.why: The for value must equal the input id.

mini.title: Contact form
mini.brief: Build a contact form with name, email, message and a submit button, all labelled.

lab.title: Form accessibility audit
lab.brief: Audit a form with missing labels, duplicate ids and an unlabelled textarea, then repair it.
milestones: List each control and its label.

title: Advanced Forms and Validation
goal: Use native constraints, grouped controls and file uploads correctly.

topics.title: Required, pattern and length constrain input
topics.body: `required`, `minlength`, `maxlength` aur `pattern` browser ko batate hain valid input kya hai. Ye UX hai, security nahi.
topics.code:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<body>
  <form>
    <label for="code">Course code</label>
    <input id="code" name="code" pattern="[A-Z]{3}[0-9]{3}" required>
  </form>
</body>
</html>

topics.title: fieldset groups related controls
topics.body: `fieldset` aur `legend` radio group ko ek naam dete hain, taaki screen reader bataye ki ye choices kis sawaal ki hain.
topics.code:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<body>
  <fieldset>
    <legend>Year</legend>
    <label><input type="radio" name="year" value="1"> First</label>
    <label><input type="radio" name="year" value="2"> Second</label>
  </fieldset>
</body>
</html>

topics.title: File uploads need the right encoding
topics.body: File input ke saath form ka `enctype="multipart/form-data"` hona chahiye, warna sirf file name bhejta hai, file nahi.
topics.code:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<body>
  <form action="/upload" method="post" enctype="multipart/form-data">
    <label for="resume">Resume</label>
    <input id="resume" name="resume" type="file" accept=".pdf">
  </form>
</body>
</html>

debug.title: Radio buttons with different names
debug.broken:
<input type="radio" name="a" value="yes">
<input type="radio" name="b" value="no">
debug.fix:
<input type="radio" name="answer" value="yes">
<input type="radio" name="answer" value="no">
debug.error: Different names put each radio in its own group, so both can be selected at once.

debug.title: A file form without multipart encoding
debug.error: Wrong encoding: the server receives only the file name instead of the file contents.

tasks.title: Validated admission form
tasks.statement: Build a form with a required name (min 3 characters), an email and a course code matching three letters and three digits.
tasks.solution:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<body>
  <form action="/admission" method="post">
    <label for="name">Name</label>
    <input id="name" name="name" type="text" minlength="3" required>
    <label for="email">Email</label>
    <input id="email" name="email" type="email" required>
    <label for="code">Course code</label>
    <input id="code" name="code" pattern="[A-Z]{3}[0-9]{3}" required>
    <button type="submit">Apply</button>
  </form>
</body>
</html>

interviewBank.q: Is native HTML validation enough for security?
interviewBank.answer: No. It improves user experience but can be bypassed by disabling JavaScript, editing the DOM or sending a direct request. The server must validate every field again.

interviewBank.q: When should an input be disabled instead of readonly?
interviewBank.answer: Readonly keeps the value submitted but prevents editing. Disabled removes the control from submission and from the tab order, so it is for values that must not be sent.

defenseBank.q: A learner’s pattern does not match and they cannot see why.
defenseBank.answer: I test the pattern against a known-good value, check the anchors, and explain that pattern is fully anchored in HTML.

defenseBank.q: Why group radios in a fieldset?
defenseBank.answer: Without a legend the group has no question attached, so a screen-reader user hears the options but not what they are choosing.

mcqBank.q: Which attribute limits the number of characters a user can type?
mcqBank.why: maxlength caps the input length.

mcqBank.q: Which enctype is required for file uploads?
mcqBank.why: Files need the multipart encoding.

mini.title: Scholarship form
mini.brief: Build a form with a radio group for year, a checkbox for consent and a validated pincode.

lab.title: Validation repair
lab.brief: Fix a form where radios are ungrouped, a file input never uploads and a pattern accepts invalid codes.
milestones: Rewrite the pattern and test it.

title: Audio and Video
goal: Embed media with controls, captions and sensible loading behaviour.

topics.title: video needs controls and a source
topics.body: `controls` player UI deta hai. `source` se multiple formats diye jaate hain aur browser pehla supported chunta hai.
topics.code:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<body>
  <video controls width="320">
    <source src="intro.mp4" type="video/mp4">
  </video>
</body>
</html>

topics.title: Captions are part of the content
topics.body: `track kind="captions"` se subtitles judte hain. Deaf users ke liye captions aur noisy environment me sabke liye useful hain.
topics.code:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<body>
  <video controls width="320">
    <source src="intro.mp4" type="video/mp4">
    <track kind="captions" src="intro.vtt" srclang="en" label="English">
  </video>
</body>
</html>

topics.title: audio uses the same source pattern
topics.body: `audio` me bhi `source` aur `controls` hote hain. Autoplay sound ke saath blocked hota hai, isliye `muted` ke bina bharosa mat karo.
topics.code:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<body>
  <audio controls>
    <source src="theme.mp3" type="audio/mpeg">
  </audio>
</body>
</html>

debug.title: A video with no controls
debug.error: No controls: the visitor cannot play, pause or seek the media.

debug.title: Autoplay with sound
debug.error: Autoplay with audio is blocked by most browsers, so the video never starts; muted autoplay is the supported pattern.

tasks.title: Embed a captioned video
tasks.statement: Create a video player 480 pixels wide with an mp4 source and an English captions track.
tasks.solution:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<body>
  <video controls width="480">
    <source src="lesson.mp4" type="video/mp4">
    <track kind="captions" src="lesson.vtt" srclang="en" label="English">
  </video>
</body>
</html>

interviewBank.q: Why does autoplay often fail?
interviewBank.answer: Browsers block audible autoplay to protect users from unexpected sound. Muted autoplay is allowed, and playsinline keeps iOS from opening fullscreen.

interviewBank.q: What does the track element add?
interviewBank.answer: Timed text tracks: captions, subtitles, descriptions or chapters, linked to the media and selectable by the user.

defenseBank.q: A learner’s video is black on iPhone.
defenseBank.answer: I check the codec and the playsinline attribute; Safari requires a supported codec and otherwise goes fullscreen.

defenseBank.q: Why are captions not optional?
defenseBank.answer: They are the text alternative for audio, and they also help in silent or noisy environments. Without them the media is inaccessible.

mcqBank.q: Which attribute shows the browser’s media controls?
mcqBank.why: controls renders play, pause and volume UI.

mcqBank.q: Which element links a caption file to a video?
mcqBank.why: track references the WebVTT file and its kind.

mini.title: Media card
mini.brief: Build a card with a short video, a caption track and a text transcript link.

lab.title: Playback debugging
lab.brief: Diagnose a video that never plays: wrong MIME type, missing controls and blocked autoplay.

title: HTML Head, Metadata and SEO
goal: Write metadata that controls the tab, sharing cards, indexing and language.

topics.title: The title and description are the search result
topics.body: `title` result ka heading banta hai aur meta description snippet. Dono page ke content ko honestly describe karein.
topics.code:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <title>HTML Course | BroCode</title>
  <meta name="description" content="Learn HTML from zero with lessons, labs and projects.">
</head>
<body></body>
</html>

topics.title: Open Graph controls the shared card
topics.body: Social platforms `og:title`, `og:description` aur `og:image` padhte hain. Inke bina link preview khaali ya random aata hai.
topics.code:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta property="og:title" content="HTML Course">
  <meta property="og:description" content="Beginner to advanced HTML.">
  <meta property="og:image" content="https://example.com/card.png">
</head>
<body></body>
</html>
topics.output: Link preview: HTML Course / Beginner to advanced HTML.

topics.title: Link resources with the right hints
topics.body: Stylesheet `link rel="stylesheet"` se aata hai. Scripts `defer` ke saath parse ke baad chalte hain, isliye render block nahi karte.
topics.code:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/style.css">
  <script src="js/app.js" defer></script>
</head>
<body></body>
</html>
topics.output: Page styled; script runs after parsing

debug.title: A relative canonical URL
debug.error: Relative canonical: crawlers need the absolute preferred URL to consolidate duplicates.

debug.title: A blocking script in the head
debug.error: Render-blocking script: the parser stops until the file downloads and runs, delaying first paint.

tasks.title: Write a shareable head
tasks.statement: Add a title, description, canonical URL, og:title, og:description and og:image.
tasks.solution:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  <title>Admissions | BroCode</title>
  <meta name="description" content="Apply for the BroCode HTML course.">
  <link rel="canonical" href="https://example.com/admissions">
  <meta property="og:title" content="Admissions | BroCode">
  <meta property="og:description" content="Apply for the HTML course.">
  <meta property="og:image" content="https://example.com/admissions.png">
</head>
<body></body>
</html>

interviewBank.q: Does the meta description affect ranking?
interviewBank.answer: Not directly. It influences the snippet users see, which affects click-through, and a misleading description is often replaced by the search engine with page text.

interviewBank.q: What is the difference between defer and async?
interviewBank.answer: Both download in parallel. defer preserves document order and runs after parsing; async runs as soon as it is ready and can execute in any order.

defenseBank.q: A shared link shows no preview image.
defenseBank.answer: I check that og:image is an absolute URL, publicly reachable and large enough for the platform’s card.

defenseBank.q: Why not put every script at the bottom?
defenseBank.answer: defer in the head achieves the same non-blocking behaviour while keeping resource declarations together and order guaranteed.
steps: Keep scripts declared in the head.

mcqBank.q: Which meta tag controls the snippet description?
mcqBank.why: The description meta supplies the search snippet.

mcqBank.q: Which attribute makes a script run after parsing in order?
mcqBank.why: defer waits for parsing and preserves order.

mini.title: SEO head checklist
mini.brief: Write a head with charset, viewport, title, description, canonical and three Open Graph tags.

lab.title: Share card test
lab.brief: Build a page with Open Graph tags and verify the preview with a link-preview tool.

title: HTML Accessibility
goal: Make pages usable with a keyboard and a screen reader using native semantics first.

topics.title: Use native elements before ARIA
topics.body: `button` pehle se focusable, clickable aur announced hai. Div par role aur keydown lagane se zyada kaam aur zyada bugs hote hain.
topics.code:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<body>
  <button type="button">Save</button>
</body>
</html>

topics.title: Every image and control needs a name
topics.body: Alt text, labels aur visible link text accessible name dete hain. Naam ke bina control screen reader ke liye "button" hi rehta hai.
topics.code:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<body>
  <label for="search">Search</label>
  <input id="search" name="q" type="search">
  <button type="submit">Go</button>
</body>
</html>

topics.title: Keyboard focus must stay visible
topics.body: Tab se sab interactive cheezein reachable honi chahiye aur focus ring dikhna chahiye. `outline: none` bina replacement ke accessibility todta hai.
topics.code:

Content

debug.title: A clickable div pretending to be a button
debug.error: Not focusable and no role: keyboard users cannot reach it, and screen readers do not announce a button.

debug.title: A form input with only a placeholder
debug.error: Placeholder as the only label: the field has no persistent accessible name once typing starts.

tasks.statement: Build a labelled search input, a submit button and a skip link to main content.
tasks.solution:

interviewBank.q: What is the first rule of ARIA?
interviewBank.answer: Do not use ARIA if a native element already provides the semantics. Native elements carry keyboard behaviour and accessibility support that a role alone does not.

interviewBank.q: What makes a focus indicator accessible?
interviewBank.answer: It must be visible against the background and not removed without an equivalent replacement. Keyboard users rely on it to know where they are.

defenseBank.q: A designer wants outline removed.
defenseBank.answer: I keep a visible custom focus style instead of removing it, because keyboard users lose their position otherwise.

defenseBank.q: How do you test accessibility without a screen reader?
defenseBank.answer: Keyboard-only navigation, the accessibility tree in dev tools and automated checks catch many issues, though a real screen-reader pass is still the reference.

mcqBank.q: Which element is keyboard accessible by default?
mcqBank.why: button is focusable and activates with Enter and Space.

mcqBank.q: What should a decorative image use?
mcqBank.why: An empty alt removes it from the accessibility tree.

mini.title: Keyboard audit
mini.brief: Tab through a page and record every element that cannot be reached or has no visible focus.

lab.title: ARIA cleanup
lab.brief: Replace three custom role divs with native elements and verify the accessibility tree.
milestones: Compare the tree before and after.

title: Iframes and Embedding
goal: Embed external content safely with titles, sandboxing and lazy loading.

topics.title: An iframe needs a title
topics.body: `title` iframe ka accessible name hai; screen reader batata hai ki embedded content kya hai. Iske bina "frame" hi sunaai deta hai.
topics.code:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<body>
  <iframe src="https://example.com/map" title="Campus map" width="600" height="400"></iframe>
</body>
</html>

topics.title: sandbox limits what the frame can do
topics.body: `sandbox` default me scripts, forms aur navigation block karta hai. Sirf jo chahiye wahi allow karo, poori permission mat do.
topics.code:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<body>
  <iframe src="https://example.com/widget" title="Widget" sandbox="allow-scripts"></iframe>
</body>
</html>

topics.title: Lazy loading keeps the first paint fast
topics.body: `loading="lazy"` iframe ko viewport ke paas aane tak load nahi karta, isliye below-the-fold embeds page ko slow nahi karte.
topics.code:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<body>
  <iframe src="https://example.com/video" title="Lesson video" loading="lazy" width="560" height="315"></iframe>
</body>
</html>
topics.output: Video embed loads when scrolled into view

debug.title: An iframe with no title
debug.error: Missing title: the frame has no accessible name, so its purpose is unknown to assistive technology.

debug.title: An iframe with no sandbox for untrusted content
debug.error: No sandbox: the embedded page runs with the full privileges its origin allows, including navigation and forms.

tasks.title: Embed a titled map
tasks.statement: Create a lazy-loaded map iframe, 600 by 400, with a descriptive title.
tasks.solution:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<body>
  <iframe src="https://example.com/map" title="Campus map" width="600" height="400" loading="lazy"></iframe>
</body>
</html>

interviewBank.q: Why is an iframe a performance and security concern?
interviewBank.answer: It loads a second document with its own resources and scripts. Without a sandbox it can navigate the top page, and it adds a network request that can delay the page.

interviewBank.q: When should content be embedded instead of linked?
interviewBank.answer: When the surrounding page needs it in context, such as a map or a video. If it is a full independent page, a link is simpler and safer.

defenseBank.q: A learner embeds an untrusted widget with scripts and forms.
defenseBank.answer: I add sandbox and allow only what the widget needs, then verify the widget still works.
steps: Grant one permission at a time.

defenseBank.q: Why add a title to every iframe?
defenseBank.answer: The title is the only thing a screen-reader user hears before entering the frame, so it must name the embedded content.

mcqBank.q: Which attribute names an iframe for assistive technology?
mcqBank.why: The title attribute supplies the frame’s accessible name.

mcqBank.q: Which attribute postpones loading until needed?
mcqBank.why: Lazy loading defers off-screen iframes.

mini.title: Safe embed card
mini.brief: Build an embed card with a sandboxed iframe, a title and a fallback link.
steps: Add a link for unsupported browsers.

lab.title: Embed hardening
lab.brief: Harden a page with two iframes: one map and one untrusted widget.

title: Advanced Native HTML Elements
goal: Use details, dialog, progress, meter, template and data elements appropriately.

topics.title: progress reports completion
topics.body: `progress` value aur max ke saath task completion dikhata hai. Iska use loading indicator aur course completion dono ke liye hota hai.
topics.code:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<body>
  <label for="done">Lessons done</label>
  <progress id="done" value="4" max="10">4 of 10</progress>
</body>
</html>

topics.title: meter shows a measurement in a range
topics.body: `meter` known range me measurement dikhata hai, jaise disk usage. `progress` task completion ke liye hai; dono ko mix mat karo.
topics.code:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<body>
  <label for="disk">Disk used</label>
  <meter id="disk" value="0.7">70%</meter>
</body>
</html>

topics.title: dialog is a native modal or popover
topics.body: `dialog` `showModal()` ke saath focus trap aur Escape handling deta hai. Custom div modal se kam code aur better accessibility.
topics.code: Need help?

debug.title: meter used for task progress
debug.error: Wrong element: meter measures a value in a known range, while progress reports completion of a task.

debug.title: A dialog opened without showModal
debug.error: Dialog never opened: the element is in the DOM but hidden until show() or showModal() is called.

tasks.title: Course progress panel
tasks.statement: Show completion with a progress element and disk usage with a meter, both labelled.
tasks.solution:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<body>
  <label for="done">Lessons done</label>
  <progress id="done" value="4" max="10">4 of 10</progress>
  <label for="disk">Disk used</label>
  <meter id="disk" value="0.7">70%</meter>
</body>
</html>

interviewBank.q: What is the difference between progress and meter?
interviewBank.answer: progress reports how much of a task is complete and may be indeterminate. meter displays a measurement inside a known range with low/high/optimum semantics.

interviewBank.q: What does the template element do?
interviewBank.answer: It holds inert markup that is not rendered or executed. Scripts clone its content when the element is actually needed.

defenseBank.q: A learner builds a modal from divs.
defenseBank.answer: The dialog element gives focus management, Escape handling and a backdrop natively, with less code to get wrong.

defenseBank.q: Why not use progress for a score?
defenseBank.answer: A score is a measurement, not task completion. meter carries the range semantics that assistive technology can announce meaningfully.

mcqBank.q: Which element reports completion of a task?
mcqBank.why: progress is defined for task completion.

mcqBank.q: Which method opens a dialog as a modal?
mcqBank.why: showModal makes it modal and manages focus.

mini.title: FAQ with details
mini.brief: Build a four-question FAQ with details, summary and one open by default.

lab.title: Native widgets pass
lab.brief: Replace a custom progress bar, a custom modal and a custom tooltip with native elements where possible.
milestones: Keep custom tooltip only if needed.

title: HTML with CSS and JavaScript
goal: Connect structure to styling and behaviour without confusing responsibilities.

topics.title: Link CSS instead of styling inline
topics.body: External stylesheet cache hoti hai aur saare pages par reuse hoti hai. Inline style sirf one-off exception ke liye.
topics.code: Styled by a file

topics.title: Scripts should not block parsing
topics.body: `defer` script ko parse ke baad chalata hai aur order preserve karta hai, isliye DOM ready milta hai.
topics.code:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<body>
  <button id="go">Go</button>
  <script src="js/app.js" defer></script>
</body>
</html>

topics.title: Data attributes connect HTML to JavaScript
topics.body: `data-*` se behaviour ke liye values HTML me rakhi jaati hain, aur script `dataset` se padhta hai. Isse markup aur logic ka contract clear rehta hai.
topics.code:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<body>
  <button data-action="save">Save</button>
</body>
</html>

debug.title: A script in the head with no defer
debug.error: Blocking script before the body: the parser stops, and if the script queries the button it runs before the element exists.

debug.title: A class used as a JavaScript id
debug.error: Mismatched hook: the element has no id, so the lookup returns null and the handler never attaches.

tasks.title: Wire a data-attribute button
tasks.statement: Create a button with data-action="save", link a deferred script and a stylesheet from the head.
tasks.solution:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="css/style.css">
  <script src="js/app.js" defer></script>
</head>
<body>
  <button type="button" data-action="save">Save</button>
</body>
</html>

interviewBank.q: Why keep CSS and JavaScript out of HTML?
interviewBank.answer: Each file has one responsibility, which makes caching, testing and reuse possible. Inline code also bypasses the content security policy and is harder to review.

interviewBank.q: What is the DOM and how does JavaScript change it?
interviewBank.answer: The DOM is the browser’s object model of the document. Scripts create, remove, move and modify nodes, and the browser re-renders the affected parts.

defenseBank.q: A learner styles everything inline for speed.
defenseBank.answer: Inline styles cannot be cached or reused and they override external rules, which makes later changes harder.

defenseBank.q: Why use data attributes instead of ids for behaviour?
defenseBank.answer: Ids must be unique and often carry styling or fragment meaning. A data attribute names the behaviour explicitly and can repeat.
steps: Keep ids for labels and fragments.

mcqBank.q: Which script attribute preserves order and waits for parsing?
mcqBank.why: defer runs after parsing in document order.

mcqBank.q: How does JavaScript read data-action?
mcqBank.why: dataset exposes data-* attributes in camelCase.

mini.title: Interactive counter
mini.brief: Build a button and output element with a deferred script that increments a counter.

lab.title: Separation refactor
lab.brief: Move inline styles and inline handlers out of a page into external files.

title: HTML Debugging, Validation and Best Practices
goal: Find and fix real markup defects with dev tools, validation and a production checklist.

topics.title: The inspector shows the parser’s result
topics.body: Browser invalid nesting ko auto-correct karta hai, isliye Elements panel aapke source se alag ho sakta hai. Difference hi bug ka clue hai.

interviewBank.q: Why does the parsed DOM differ from the source?
interviewBank.answer: The parser applies error recovery to invalid markup, closing or moving elements to produce a valid tree. The inspector shows that repaired result.

interviewBank.q: What does the W3C validator check?
interviewBank.answer: Conformance to the HTML standard: syntax, allowed nesting, required attributes and duplicate attributes. It does not check visual design or accessibility completeness.

defenseBank.q: A page looks fine but fails validation.
defenseBank.answer: The browser repaired the markup, which may still break scripts or assistive technology. I fix the source rather than relying on recovery.

defenseBank.q: How do you debug a layout that shifts?
defenseBank.answer: I check image dimensions, late-loading embeds and fonts, then reserve space so the layout does not move.

mcqBank.q: What does the HTML validator check?
mcqBank.why: It checks syntax and allowed structure, not design.

mcqBank.q: Which practice prevents layout shift from images?
mcqBank.why: Reserved space stops content from jumping when the image loads.

interviewBank.q: How do you structure a multi-page site in plain HTML?
interviewBank.answer: Give every page the same header, nav, main and footer, link pages with relative URLs and keep shared assets in predictable folders. The main region changes per page.

interviewBank.q: What would you check before calling a site production ready?
interviewBank.answer: Valid markup, one main landmark, unique titles and descriptions, labelled controls, alt text, working links, responsive images and a keyboard pass.

defenseBank.q: A learner wants to skip the checklist to ship faster.
defenseBank.answer: The checklist is the cheapest test we have; fixing a broken form or missing label after launch costs far more.

defenseBank.q: How do you review an HTML project?
defenseBank.answer: Structure first, then semantics, then accessibility, then validity, and only then visual polish.
steps: Validate and test with the keyboard.
